harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up nginx on node1 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using a locally-signed leaf certificate that is automatically renewed before expiry (via a systemd timer + renewal script) and picked up via `systemctl reload nginx`, verified continuous availability across a live renewal, and completed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol confirming the automation and service persist across reboot.
actions_performed: Installed openssl and nginx via dnf on node1 (RHEL 10)
Built a local demo CA at /etc/pki/rotation-ca (ca.key/ca.crt, index.txt, serial, openssl ca config with req_leaf section and SANs for node1/127.0.0.1/NODE_IP)

Wrote /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh: checks cert expiry with `openssl x509 -checkend`, and if within 180s of expiry generates a new 6-minute-validity leaf cert via `openssl ca -enddate`, atomically installs it to /etc/nginx/certs/{server.crt,server.key} with correct ownership/SELinux context, then runs `systemctl reload nginx` (graceful, no dropped listener) and logs the new expiry via logger
Added /etc/nginx/conf.d/rotation-tls.conf serving HTTPS on 8443 with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at the managed cert files
Opened firewalld port 8443/tcp permanently and reloaded
Enabled+started nginx; generated the initial cert; verified curl HTTPS success with SAN/chain validation against the CA
Created systemd unit cert-renew.service + cert-renew.timer (OnBootSec=30s, OnUnitActiveSec=30s) and enabled the timer

Ran a 2-second-interval curl probe loop against the HTTPS endpoint spanning an automatic renewal event: 85/85 requests returned 200, cert serial changed 1000->1001 and notAfter extended, with zero failed requests
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, nginx/timer active, cert serial/dates, HTTPS 200)
Issued `systemctl reboot` via a backgrounded delayed command so the ack returned before disconnection, polled node1 until exec was available again
Confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime after reboot, confirmed nginx and cert-renew.timer active+enabled, confirmed firewall port persisted, confirmed HTTPS still returns 200

Waited through a full renewal cycle post-reboot and confirmed a second automatic renewal occurred (serial 1001->1002, notAfter extended) while HTTPS kept returning 200, proving the renewal automation persists across restart
Cleaned up temporary probe/test files on node1

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 on node1 with a valid, verifiable certificate
evidence.summary: nginx started/enabled and firewalld port 8443 opened; curl -v against https://node1:8443 with --cacert shows full chain validation, SAN match, and HTTP/1.1 200 OK response

evidence.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
evidence.summary: Initial cert (serial=1000, notAfter 03:24:35) issued by renew-cert.sh; cert-renew.timer enabled and firing every 30s; at 03:22:00 (before the 03:24:35 expiry) the timer-triggered service automatically renewed the cert to serial=1001 with new notAfter 03:28:00, confirmed via journalctl log entry and openssl x509 output

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime during rotation)
evidence.summary: A 2-second polling probe against https://node1:8443 spanning the 03:22:00 renewal logged serial flipping from 1000 to 1001 mid-stream with 85/85 requests returning http_code=200 and 0 failures, proving nginx's `systemctl reload` picked up the new cert without dropping traffic

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline before reboot
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=739c9792-2418-47cc-a875-95b27428f3fc, uptime since 23:15:29, nginx and cert-renew.timer active, valid cert serial=1001, and HTTPS returning 200 immediately before triggering reboot

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: reboot acknowledgement returns before disconnect, then node becomes reachable again with changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command backgrounded with a short delay so its ack returned before the connection dropped; subsequent exec calls failed with connection reset/timeout while node1 was down; polling succeeded once it came back, showing a new boot_id=c736699c-ee12-4dd9-9411-4dfb945094ad and fresh uptime start of 23:22:31, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: post-restart recovery of required services and automation, including a subsequent automatic renewal proving persistence
evidence.summary: After reboot, nginx and cert-renew.timer are both active and enabled, firewall port 8443 persisted, and HTTPS returns 200 again; the timer resumed its schedule and, without any manual intervention, performed a second live renewal (serial 1001->1002, notAfter extended to 03:31:20) while HTTPS continued returning 200, confirming the auto-renewal setup survives a reboot
